UI-09 (light/dark theme toggle + persistence): web/src/theme.ts, a data-theme attribute on <html> cycling Auto/Light/Dark, persisted to localStorage (wrapped in try/catch), applied as early as possible in main.ts (before mount()) to avoid a flash of the wrong theme on a returning visit. Layered ON TOP OF style.css's existing passive prefers-color-scheme support rather than replacing it -- the media-query block is now guarded by :root:not([data-theme='light']) so an explicit light choice can still override a dark OS. The toggle lives outside app.ts's screen-swapping (mount() replaces #app's content wholesale on every screen transition) via a new #pw-theme-toggle sibling to #app in index.html, mounted once from main.ts, so it and the chosen theme persist across every screen. One real bug found by the Playwright suite itself, not by inspection: a first design used position:fixed to float the toggle in a screen corner, which at the test browser's window width sat exactly on top of the viewer toolbar's rightmost buttons and silently ate clicks meant for 'Compare' -- four previously-passing UI-05 tests started failing the moment this was added, each with Playwright's own error naming the intercepting element. Fixed by making body a flex column with #pw-theme-toggle as a real in-flow reserved strip (flex: 0 0 auto) above #app (flex: 1 1 auto; min-height: 0) rather than a floating overlay -- in-flow layout can't collide with anything below it at any window width, which position:fixed can't guarantee. 4 new Playwright tests: toggle visible before any document is open (proves it survives screen swaps), cycling through all three states, an explicit dark choice actually changing a computed CSS variable (not just the attribute), and persistence across a reload. No backend touched at all this session.

openQuestions: UI-09's theme toggle is a 3-state cycle (Auto/Light/Dark), not a simple 2-state light/dark switch -- deliberately preserves the pre-existing passive OS-preference support as a real, chooseable option ('Auto') rather than discarding it once an explicit toggle was added. Any future change to this cycle order or the LABELS record in theme.ts should keep 'system' as a real, reachable state, not just an implicit default.

A fixed-position UI element anywhere in this app's layout is now a known risk, not just a one-off -- confirmed twice in this session's history (the theme toggle over the Compare button) that CSS position:fixed content can silently overlap and eat clicks on whatever happens to be underneath at a given window width, and Playwright's own actionability-wait failure (naming the exact intercepting element) is what caught it, not visual inspection. Prefer real in-flow layout (flexbox/grid reserved space) over position:fixed for any future persistent UI chrome in this app.

Any Playwright test that acts on the UI immediately after an action whose visible effect resolves BEFORE the full async chain behind it settles needs to wait for that chain's actual last effect, not an intermediate one -- confirmed twice in the UI-08 session (once in _commit_edit itself, once one step further in the same test's own undo-then-redo sequence: reloadDocument() re-renders content before it refreshes the history panel that re-enables the Redo button). page.click()'s own actionability wait happens to absorb this class of race for a plain button click; a raw page.keyboard.press() never does. Any future test chaining a keyboard shortcut after a document-changing action needs an explicit wait for the specific state the shortcut depends on (e.g. a button's enabled state), not just the action's most visible symptom.

ALWAYS run `python3 -m ruff format --check engine cli tools tests server` as part of the local gate, not just `python3 -m ruff check .` -- these are two separate CI 'lint' job steps and only running the first one left a real formatting violation undetected for a full push-and-fail cycle earlier this session.

isTypingTarget (viewer.ts) checks `target.isContentEditable`, not just INPUT/TEXTAREA tag names -- the correct general check for 'is the user typing somewhere', since isContentEditable is true for a contenteditable element AND its descendants. Any FUTURE editable UI surface gets this guard for free as long as it's built on contenteditable or a real INPUT/TEXTAREA.

UI-08's keyboard shortcuts are deliberately NOT documented anywhere in the UI itself (no shortcuts-help modal) -- only via each button's title/aria-label. Matches the feature's S-sizing; worth revisiting if user feedback says shortcuts aren't discoverable enough.

UI-05's diff overlay is computed client-side with a per-channel tolerance of 24 (web/src/compare.ts's CHANNEL_TOLERANCE) -- empirical, not derived from engine/verify.py's DEFAULT_TOLERANCE (a different kind of threshold entirely).

UI-05's 'before' image is always the document exactly as first opened (UndoRedoJournal.original_bytes), never 'the state before the most recent edit'. FNT-12 (already built) is the per-edit-diff feature, a different thing.

UI-04's history panel shows only what was requested (an Op's own fields), never the EditResult each op produced -- tier, confidence, verification are NOT part of GET .../history's response. Documented in history.ts's module docstring.

mypy must be run scoped to `engine cli tools server` (matching .github/workflows), never over the whole tree -- running it over `tests/` too surfaces ~240 pre-existing errors in test files never meant to be strictly typed.

PyMuPDF's Document.tobytes() is NOT idempotent even with zero document changes between calls -- regenerates a random component of the PDF's /ID array on every call. Compare parsed content (get_text(), page_count, rendered PNG bytes), never raw PDF bytes, in any test.

pip-audit in this sandbox flags CVEs in cryptography/httplib2/pip/pyjwt/setuptools/urllib3/wheel -- none are pdfworkerz's own dependencies. Sandbox environment drift, not something a code change here introduces or can fix.

UI-02's click-to-edit overlay approximates the font family/weight/style shown while editing rather than loading the document's actual embedded font as a browser @font-face -- documented in web/README.md.

overlay.ts's cancelEdit() has a documented reentrancy fix (contentEditable=false can synchronously fire blur, re-entering cancelEdit) -- preserve the 'clear shared state before touching the box' ordering in any future edit.

ReplaceTextOp (search-based) must never be reused for a UI action that targets one specific span the user clicked -- it edits every occurrence of the matched text on the page. ReplaceSpanTextOp (index-based) is what click-to-edit uses instead.

PreviewTextOp/PageSpansOp/render_original_page are read-only and deliberately never journaled -- applied directly in server/app.py. Any FUTURE read-only Op or route should follow the same direct-apply pattern.
viewer.ts's reloadDocument rebuilds the ENTIRE thumbnail rail rather than invalidating just the current page's thumbnail -- a deliberately accepted minor inefficiency, not a bug.

server/app.py's CORSMiddleware is scoped to a loopback-origin regex -- deliberately permissive on port since auth here is a header a browser never auto-attaches. Revisit before ever adding cookie-based or credentialed auth.
web/package.json pins pdfjs-dist==6.3.289 deliberately: versions >=5.6.83 <6.2.108 carry a public high-severity CVE. Re-run npm audit by hand after ever changing this pin.
web/src/polyfills.ts + web/src/pdf.worker.ts work around a real Map/WeakMap.prototype.getOrInsertComputed gap on this sandbox's pinned Playwright test browser.
tests/web/'s Playwright tests build on a *built* web/dist, never `vite dev` -- if web/dist doesn't exist, the whole module is skipped (not failed).
